Africa goes eVTOL, C-UAS Raises, and In-Orbit Software Updates

Daily Hard Tech Headlines:

- Nanoprecise Sci Corp has raised a $38M Series C. The Alberta-based startup focuses on industrial maintenance technology.

- Ethiopian Airlines has agreed to a $30M deal with @ArcherAviation. The deal “will primarily focus on supporting the initial deployment of our aircraft to develop an air taxi network on the continent, while exploring other use cases, including eco-tourism.”

- @allencontrol has announced a $30M Series A. The round was led by Craft Ventures, with participation from Inspired Capital and Rally Ventures. The funding will help ACS scale the deployment of their Bullfrog C-UAS systems. Bullfrog boosts traditional weapon accuracy with AI, computer vision, and proprietary control systems, turning them into precision-targeting systems.

- @torcrobotics, Flextronics International Ltd., and @nvidia are joining forces to build out the Onboard AI hardware platform for self-driving trucks. Torc develops autonomy-enabling technology such as radar, lidar, and computer vision.

- Thales has partnered with Dedrone by Axon. The partnership focuses on outfitting Thales’ tactical vehicles with a C-UAS system developed by Dedrone.

- SpearUAV, the Israeli defense company developing munition, UAS technology, and more, has raised funding led by Deep Insight venture fund. The funding amount was not disclosed.

- Oshkosh Defense, based in Wisconsin, has showcased its rocket system that can be mounted onto a vehicle.

- @Albedo has announced the “first on-orbit software update for Clarity-1,” their satellite.

- Schneider Electric has announced a $700M investment into its American manufacturing operations, which will create 1,000 new jobs.

- Vattenfall, the Swedish energy company, has announced the development of Germany's largest offshore wind farm. Construction is slated to begin in 2026.

tweets.text:
my first entry into @doodles came after a conversation with @SeanPRobb about building on @flow_blockchain . i was part of a startup at the time trying to bring kids content onchain and sean was incredibly generous with his time and insights on how we might do this. doodles had recently launched D2 on flow and it seemed like an ecosystem i was meant to be a part of.

eventually, D2 migrated to @base - same thesis ("crypto for the masses"), different pathway. i lamented the loss of my original reason for joining the community, but by that time i was already hooked. so much so that i bought another dood: this time, a pickle that i had bookmarked for months. why the pickle? i had started writing a story series about a pickle based on improvised bedtime stories my kids loved. my idea was to eventually create something using this doodles IP.

this was all before the summer of 2024. holy shit! do you remember the sheer number of partnerships, music collaborations, animations, film festivals, store takeovers, merch, and product releases? the doodles team was on an absolute tear. the funny thing is, though, it felt less likely during all that activity that my pickle story could find its place in the world. i was ecstatic to be on the thrill ride, but at the same time it didn't feel like it was my IP to use.

today, i think, marks a full-circle moment to me joining doodles in the first place. i don't know all the ins and outs of what dreamnet is, but i have a feeling my pickle story will finally find its home there.
